In general, the UK’s asylum seeking policy is too strict and should be made easier to enter the country. The current system is inefficient and bureaucratic, and the amount of red tape required of those who wish to enter the country legally also leads people who want to migrate to do so in ways that are unsafe and dangerous, such as through boat crossings, so improving the asylum system would also help curb illegal migration. In general, the UK’s asylum seeking policy is in need of reform. The current system is too slow and inefficient, leading to people waiting in limbo for years while their cases are processed. This is unfair to those who are waiting, and also leads to people taking dangerous illegal routes to enter the country. There is also a need to improve the system for asylum seekers who have been granted leave to remain in the UK, as there is currently a lack of support for these people to integrate into society. However, the UK should not make it easier to enter the country, as this would lead to an increase in the number of people coming to the UK and a greater strain on the system for processing applications. Instead, the government should focus on improving the current system and making it more efficient.

There should be changes to the current asylum seeking policy in the UK. The current system is inhumane, and does not allow people to seek asylum in a fair way. The current system is also very inefficient, and does not allow people to seek asylum in a timely way. There should be legal routes open to the UK for all asylum seekers and there should be more energy directed into these issues rather than empty and unworkable PR stunts about 'Stopping The Boats.' As a developed country and a democratic country I feel that we have a moral obligation to make routes open to those with genuine reasons to flee their own countries. We pride ourselves on our democracy and our 'civilised' status and yet we demonise people who are amongst the most vulnerable in the world. While we cannot welcome everyone who has a wish to come here, we should be able to establish a fair and workable system of legal routes to give asylum to those who need it and who are entitled to it.
